text.p: These are the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Clerides and Attorney-general Markides will assign committees to draw up legal documents on all aspects of Cyprus problem and present them to United Nations by December 31.
- Water reserves in Cyprus depleting rapidly while heavy rains cause floods in parts of Europe.
- U.N. special envoy to Cyprus Diego Cordovez says gap in positions of Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides is still enormous.
- Centre-left wing presidential candidate Marios Eliades says his election manifesto will be ready soon.
- Communist Akel urges Justice Ministry to revoke decision assigning 4000 reservist commandos to police duties along ceasefire line.
- U.S. presidential emissary on Cyprus Richard Holbrooke reveals he would prefer "merger" of talks on Cyprus issue with those of Cyprus's accession to European Union.
- Economy is following "wait and see" attitude in view of Cyprus talks.
- United Nations adopts new approach on Cyprus, placing emphasis on cultivating good climate and proceeding in stages.
